title: Burst token timestamp drift causing cross-mode quota blackouts
creator: Linus Chen
description: Customer escalations from multiple tenants (hosted and private) observed sustained 429s and degraded throughput after a release to the quota orchestration service. Symptoms: sudden refusal of burst tokens, rapid quota depletion despite low request rates for some tenants, and asymmetric behavior across Dedicated pools vs Hosted. Initial logs pointed to mismatch between proxy-side token buckets and orchestrator epoch state after an upgrade that changed how 'refill_timestamp' was serialized for reserved capacity. This ticket tracks triage, hotfix, and rollout of a permanent fix plus follow-on reliability work.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy orchestration version vruntime-1.19.3 with the new token-serialization change to a staging private cluster
2) Seed tenant with reserved capacity and send low steady traffic with periodic bursts
3) Observe proxy reports of token underflow and orchestrator showing credits present in DB; proxies return 429 with 'burst_unavailable' reason
4) Reproduce on Dedicated pool by applying same binary and cheaper instance types to accelerate timing differences.
root_cause_summary: A serialization-change in the quota orchestration service accidentally switched the 'refill_timestamp' field from epoch_millis to epoch_seconds in a narrow code-path used by Dedicated/Private handshake. This led to proxies interpreting future timestamps as stale (timestamp drift ~1000x), causing them to zero out local burst buckets during reconciliation. The mismatch manifested only when proxies and orchestrator had divergent versioning (hosted rolling upgrade overlap) plus an edge-case in the token cache TTL which prevented automatic recovery until a reconciliation interval elapsed.
mitigation_actions: Roll back serialization change on orchestration service (vruntime-1.19.3 -> vruntime-1.19.2) in Hosted region us-west-2 (rolled out 2026-03-10 22:30 UTC)
Applied emergency config flag proxy.allow-stale-refill=true to Dedicated customer pools to avoid local zeroing while full fix is validated
Opened temporary throttle-relax policy for affected tenants to reduce customer-facing 429s (applied 2026-03-11 01:15 UTC)
Monitored token metrics and error rates until proxies re-synced; validated traffic recovery for top 5 affected customers
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/8897 (defensive parsing and added telemetry for refill_timestamp mismatches)
